questiontext.text: A pairing heap is best characterized as a...

feedback.text: Correct — one heap-ordered tree that restructures itself as operations run.
No — it is a self-adjusting heap, not a balanced BST.
That describes a binary heap, not a pairing heap.
No — that is a binomial heap; a pairing heap is a single multiway tree.

generalfeedback.text: A pairing heap is a single heap-ordered multiway tree that is self-adjusting: it does no explicit balancing, restructuring only during operations, which keeps it simple and fast in practice.

questiontext.text: What is the cost of merge (meld) of two pairing heaps?

feedback.text: Correct — merge just links the root with the larger key under the other root.
No — merge is O(1); extract-min is the O(log n) amortized one.
No — merging is a single constant-time link.
No — merge is O(1).

generalfeedback.text: Melding compares the two roots and makes the larger-key root a child of the smaller — a single O(1) link. Insert is merge with a one-node heap, also O(1).

questiontext.text: What is the amortized cost of extract-min in a pairing heap?

feedback.text: Correct — remove the root, then pair up and merge the children, O(log n) amortized.
No — insert and merge are O(1), but extract-min is O(log n) amortized.
No — the amortized cost is O(log n).
No — the amortized bound is O(log n).

generalfeedback.text: Extract-min deletes the root and then combines the orphaned children — the "pairing" pass that gives the structure its name — in O(log n) amortized time.

questiontext.text: How do pairing heaps compare with Fibonacci heaps in practice?

answer.text: Simpler to implement and often faster in real use, despite weaker proven bounds

feedback.text: Correct — their simplicity and low constants usually win in practice.

answer.text: More complex to implement and always slower

feedback.text: No — pairing heaps are the simpler and typically faster of the two.
No — they are structurally different and pairing heaps have lower overhead.
No — pairing heaps work with any comparable keys.

generalfeedback.text: Pairing heaps trade some theoretical guarantees for simplicity and low constant factors, so they typically outperform Fibonacci heaps in real workloads.

questiontext.text: The exact amortized complexity of decrease-key in pairing heaps was a long-standing open problem.

feedback.text: Correct — its precise decrease-key bound resisted analysis for years, though it is very fast in practice.
It is true — the tight decrease-key bound was open for a long time.

questiontext.text: Inserting a new element into a pairing heap takes O(1) time.

feedback.text: Correct — insert is just an O(1) meld with a single-node heap.
Insert is O(1): it melds the new node with the existing root.

questiontext.text: The self-adjusting heap whose extract-min combines children in a "two-at-a-time" pass is the ______ heap. (one word)

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
